questions.question: When is a subset $\boldsymbol{E}$ closed?
questions.explanation: A set $E$ is closed when it contains all of its boundary points, i.e., $\partial E\subseteq E$. Equivalently, $E$ contains every limit of convergent sequences from $E$.
questions.source_support: Definition of closed set via boundary points.
questions.polish_notes: Quality round 9: rebalanced correct-answer positions to remove option-index guessing cue
option_explanations: $\partial E\cap E=\varnothing$ means $E$ contains none of its boundary, which is the condition for being open, not closed.
$E=\varnothing$ is one example of a closed set, but not the only one; $[0,1]$ is also closed.
Having no interior points is unrelated to being closed; e.g., $\{0\}$ is closed with empty interior.
questions.rewrite_notes: Hand-authored explanation + per-option explanations (why each wrong option is wrong + the likely misread).

questions.question: If a set includes some but not all of its boundary points, how is it classified?
questions.explanation: If $E$ includes some but not all of its boundary points, then it fails both conditions: it is not open (it contains some boundary) and not closed (it misses some boundary). So it is neither.
questions.source_support: Definition of neither open nor closed.

questions.question: What is the relationship between openness and complements stated?

$\boldsymbol{E}$ is open if and only if $\boldsymbol{E}^{\complement}$ is open.
$\boldsymbol{E}$ is closed if and only if $\boldsymbol{E}^{\complement} = \boldsymbol{E}$.

questions.question: In a metric space, what does the sequential closedness criterion say about a closed set $\boldsymbol{F}$?
options: Every convergent sequence in $\boldsymbol{F}$ has its limit in $\boldsymbol{F}$.
Every sequence in $\boldsymbol{X}$ has its limit in $\boldsymbol{F}$.
No sequence in $\boldsymbol{F}$ can have a limit.

It has exactly one boundary point.
It is open only under the discrete metric.

questions.question: What does the discrete metric example show about open and closed sets?
options: Only the empty set is open.
Only singleton sets are closed, and no other sets are open.
Every set is both open and closed.
questions.explanation: In the discrete metric, every subset is both open and closed (clopen). Every singleton is an open ball, so every set is a union of open balls (open); and every set's complement is also open, so every set is closed.
questions.source_support: Example under the discrete metric.
